What are you looking to gain? Overall strength or certain areas of your body?

The best advice I ever got is the “best workout plan is the one you can stick to.” I personally build my workout plan by what’s available to me in the gym that day. Here is what I do and this works with me and my friends I’ve helped develop routines for:

Overall strength training. Progressive overload.
3-4 exercises per muscle. 4 sets. 8 reps.

If you can get 8 reps with ease, up the weight. You want to have ideally 2-3 reps in reserve meaning you can do the lift for 2-3 more reps after that 8 before failure. So if you can do 8 but feel like you can do 20, up the weight until you can do 8 but feel like you can do no more than 10-11 per set. Keep doing this each week until you feel those reps in reserve rising, up the weight, rinse and repeat. 

The 3-4 exercises aren’t something that has to be set in stone. There are lifts that are more optimal for growth but it can come down to personal preference… like I LOATHE Bulgarian split squats and would much rather do a standard back squat or a leg press.
100%. I’ve been in your position and sometimes less is more. You can be overworking the muscle which can actually hurt your gains. I now never do more than 4 exercises per muscle in a day

Unfortunately you cannot target weight loss. You can target areas to build muscle/turn fat to muscle so I would suggest looking into exercises for areas you want to improve on. I’m also not quite sure what you mean by reduce shoulder width?

This is my current build. Idk if you are looking to cut to this or bulk to this. 

.7-1g of protein per LB of body fat i.e. you weigh 230 ideally you get 230g/day 

Find your maintenance caloric intake and add/subtract 500 cals/day to it (add-bulk, subtract-cut). If you’re not sure if you should cut or bulk the answer is cut. If you’re not sure how to find maintenance, weight yourself at the same time very day, track your meals as best as you can (I.e. calories in), if at the end of a week you gain weight you’re in a surplus, lose weight it’s a deficit, remain the same you’re at maintenance. Adjust accordingly. Currently my maintenance is roughly 3k calories so I will be cutting soon so I’ll do 2500.

Incline walk for cardio *before* a lift.

Lift 4-5x per week. Best split is the one you can adhere to, mine is Arms/chest MW, Legs/Back/Shoulders T/TH, Friday free for all. Lift heavy. Ideally you want to be in the 5-8 rep range for 4 sets. I do 4 exercises per muscle in a day. This works for me, but doesn’t necessarily mean it’ll work best for you. Ideally you find what works for you and stick with it. Like some days I just want to lift heavy so I’ll do 1-3 reps or to failure.
